title: Low-Glare Tone Palette and Component Isolation for Compact Data Surfaces
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Compact data surfaces (dense tables, sparklines, chip lists) in dark and dim console themes are showing distracting high-contrast accents and harsh highlights under brand-tinted tokens. This leads to visual fatigue on prolonged dashboards and causes important micro-visuals (sparklines, cell borders, tiny action icons) to appear either washed out or too aggressive depending on brand variance.

Goal: Design a low-glare tone palette and a set of token isolation rules so small components retain legibility and hierarchy without amplifying brand tint, while larger components and brand-heavy surfaces preserve brand identity. The outcome should be a token mapping and a small set of component overrides that are easy to apply, test, and roll out behind a feature flag for early customers of Dedicated and Private deployments.
design_decision_summary: Introduce a ‘low-glare’ token family (lg-surface, lg-ink, lg-accent) that clamps chroma and reduces highlight luminance for components marked as 'compact-data-surface'. Provide component-level isolation rules for tables (zebra + micro-border), sparklines (anchored neutral accent), buttons (ghost/low-glare variants), and chart accents (muted stroke/filled variants). Map existing brand tokens to low-glare counterparts via deterministic interpolation so rollout can be automated per-brand at build time.
tradeoffs: Creates additional token family increasing token surface area; mitigated by strict naming pattern and generation scripts.
May slightly reduce brand saturation on micro-components — acceptable because brand identity is preserved on larger canvases and headers.
Requires QA across client-managed brand overrides; chosen approach favors deterministic programmatic mapping rather than manual per-brand design work to reduce ongoing maintenance cost.
acceptance_criteria: Token family 'lg-*' implemented in token registry with documentation and examples.

Component overrides for Table (compact rows), Sparkline, Small Button, and Mini-Chart validated in Storybook with dark/dim/light; visual diffs under 3% pixel delta for approved baseline (see visual-tests PR).
A migration script exists to generate low-glare token mappings from brand palettes and is included in the design-token repo.
Design review sign-off from Accessibility (contrast audit) and Product; accessibility checks recorded in issue comments.
Implementation gated behind feature flag 'theme.lowGlare' with rollout plan and telemetry for usage rates and error spikes.
Performance: no runtime color calculations in client; server precompiles tokens to CSS variables at build time for Dedicated/Private packaging.
notes_and_links: Customer forum thread referencing glare feedback: https://customers.redwood.ai/threads/11234
comments: 2025-02-12 Maya Chen: Initial proposal posted. Attached Figma frames showing dense table before/after and sparkline anchor examples. Asked ENG and A11Y for early input.
2025-02-13 Omar Reyes: Suggest we prefer precompiled CSS variables to avoid runtime cost on Private installs. Asked for token generation script to be idempotent and reversible.
2025-02-14 A11Y (Leah Patel): Ran quick contrast audit on proposed lg-ink values. Small controls pass AA with 3% margin. Recommended raising lg-ink on <10px icons. See notes in Confluence.

2025-02-16 Frontend (Jamal Ortiz): Implementation notes: will expose data-surface attribute and a CSS mapping layer. Will need a migration ticket to update existing table components to opt into compact-data-surface.
2025-02-18 PM (Evelyn Park): Agreed with feature-flag rollout; requested telemetry for metrics: adoption rate, visual-diff failures, user feedback link.

2025-02-20 Design Review (Panel): Approved with small change: reduce lg-accent saturation on green and cyan families by additional 8% to avoid perceived glow on OLED displays. Omar to update generation script.
ui_tokens_changes: Add lg-surface-0..4: neutral low-luminance surfaces for compact contexts.
Add lg-ink-strong and lg-ink-muted with tightened contrast clamps for micro-typography and icons.
Add lg-accent-neutralized variants per brand: generated by blending brand-accent with neutral-10 at 28% interpolation.
Define 'compact-data-surface' boolean meta-token used by component layer to pick lg-* tokens.
implementation_notes: Frontend will add data attribute data-surface='compact' to table, sparkline, and compact button wrappers.
Design-tokens pipeline will output :root CSS variables for both standard and lg token families during build; Dedicated/Private packaging picks desired set.
Migration: create ENG ticket to opt-in all existing compact table instances; keep fallback to legacy tokens for 2 release cycles.
Feature flag 'theme.lowGlare' controlled in Console experiments. Telemetry event 'theme.lowGlare.adopted' to measure opt-ins.
accessibility_notes: Target AA contrast ratios for text >= 4.5:1 for body small text and 3:1 for iconography where 12px+.
Audit log attached in Confluence page showing pixel-level checks for table cell text and sparkline endpoints.
Special-case: for low-vision mode, bypass low-glare and use high-contrast token set; add guard in token selection logic.
